# Collated LIKE examples and semantics from
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/operators.md

SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') LIKE COLLATE('%foo%', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT 'Foo' LIKE COLLATE('%foo%', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') NOT LIKE '%foo%'
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('Foo_', 'und:ci') LIKE COLLATE('%foo\\_%', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

# Recorded BigQuery answer: unescaped underscores match under und:ci, contrary to
# the error example in third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/operators.md.
SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') LIKE '%f_o%'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') LIKE COLLATE('%foo%', 'binary')
=> error:

SELECT COLLATE('MASSE', 'und:ci') LIKE '%Maße%'
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('\u3042', 'und:ci') LIKE COLLATE('%\u30A2%', 'und:ci')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('\u0061\u030A', 'und:ci') LIKE '%\u00C5%'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('\u0083', 'und:ci') LIKE ''
=> "true"

# No wildcards compares whole strings under the operation's collation.
SELECT COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci') LIKE 'foo'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('MASSE', 'und:ci') LIKE 'Maße'
=> "false"

SELECT COLLATE('', 'und:ci') LIKE '%'
=> "true"

# Quantified LIKE propagates the operation's collation to every comparison.
SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') LIKE ALL ('a', 'A')
=> "true"

SELECT 'a' LIKE ALL (COLLATE('a', 'und:ci'), 'A')
=> "true"

SELECT 'a' LIKE ALL ('%A%', COLLATE('a', 'und:ci'))
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') LIKE ANY ('B', 'A')
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') LIKE SOME ('B', 'C')
=> "false"

# Escaped wildcard examples from GoogleSQL compliance/functions_testlib_like.cc,
# GetFunctionTestsLikeWithCollation.
SELECT COLLATE('%barfoobar', 'und:ci') LIKE r'\%BarFoo%'
=> "true"

SELECT COLLATE('barfoobar', 'und:ci') LIKE r'\_Foo%'
=> "false"

# Removing the collation restores binary LIKE.
SELECT COLLATE(COLLATE('Foo', 'und:ci'), '') LIKE '%foo%'
=> "false"

# Recorded BigQuery answers: a collated NULL value propagates NULL, but a literal
# NULL pattern is rejected. The NULL value differs from the plain LIKE error
# example in third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/operators.md.
SELECT COLLATE(NULL, 'und:ci') LIKE 'a%'
=> null

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') LIKE NULL
=> error:

SELECT COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') LIKE CONCAT('a', CHR(92))
=> error: LIKE pattern ends with a backslash which is not allowed: a\

# Conditional expressions do not evaluate a failing LIKE branch.
SELECT IF(FALSE, COLLATE('a', 'und:ci') LIKE CONCAT('a', CHR(92)), TRUE)
=> "true"
